newsitem.title: USA: USDA SEEKS COMMENT ON EXPORT CREDIT FACILITY PLAN.
newsitem.headline: USDA SEEKS COMMENT ON EXPORT CREDIT FACILITY PLAN.

text.p: The U.S. Department of Agriculture on Friday asked for public comment on a new program intended to boost demand for U.S. agricultural goods by helping build overseas storage and processing facilities.

"By supporting such facilities, we will enhance sales of U.S. agricultural commodities and products to emerging markets where the demand for them may be constricted due to inadequate storage, processing, or handling capabilities," USDA General Sales Manager Chris Goldthwait said in a statement.
USDA published an interim final rule Friday in the Federal Register outlining the "Facility Guarantee Program."
Under the program, USDA will guarantee loans made by financial institutions for construction of facilities.
USDA provides similiar credit guarantees to help foreign customers buy U.S farm goods.
Before USDA will extend the facility loan guarantees, applicants must demonstrate that the new projects will primarily benefit U.S. agricultural exports.

Possible projects under the new program include improving a port's ability to handle and store imported U.S. grain; expanding the capacity of a feed compounding plant; supporting the sale of refrigeration equipment to a cold-storage warehouse; or providing animal health products and/or veterinary services to livestock companies, USDA said.

Public comments on the interim rule must be submitted in writing on or before October 7, 1997, to L.T. McElvain, Director, CCC Operations Division, Foreign Agricultural Service, U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), 1400 Independence Ave., SW, Stop 1035, Washington, DC 20250-1035.
